# Load libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Load the data
df <- read.csv("/Users/diyabhat/Downloads/STAT240/Project/student_lifestyle_dataset 2.csv")

# 2. Create the categories and calculate averages
summary_df <- df %>%
  # Create bins: (4,6], (6,8], (8,10]
  mutate(Sleep_Category = cut(Sleep_Hours_Per_Day, 
                              breaks = c(4, 6, 8, 10), 
                              labels = c("4-6 hrs", "6-8 hrs", "8-10 hrs"))) %>%
  # Group by the new category
  group_by(Sleep_Category) %>%
  # Calculate the average GPA for each group
  summarise(Avg_GPA = mean(GPA, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  # To draw a trendline, we need a numeric ID for the categories (1, 2, 3)
  mutate(Category_Index = as.numeric(Sleep_Category))

# 3. Create the graph
ggplot(summary_df, aes(x = Category_Index, y = Avg_GPA)) +
  # Adds the average GPA points
  geom_point(size = 5, color = "steelblue") +
  
  # Adds the linear trendline across the averages
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", se = FALSE, linetype = "dashed") +
  
  # Replace the numeric index back with your category labels
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:3, labels = summary_df$Sleep_Category) +
  
  # Formatting
  labs(title = "Average GPA by Sleep Hours Category",
       subtitle = "The red line shows the overall trend between groups",
       x = "Hours of Sleep Category",
       y = "Mean GPA") +
  theme_minimal()
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

# Load the necessary library
library(ggplot2)

# Load your dataset
# Make sure the .csv file is in your current R working directory
data <- read.csv("/Users/diyabhat/Downloads/STAT240/Project/student_lifestyle_dataset 2.csv")

# 1. Create the sleep categories (Binning)
# breaks: defines the boundaries for the bins
# labels: the names for each bin
# right = FALSE: creates intervals like [4, 5), meaning 5.0 goes into the "5-6" group
data$Sleep_Category <- cut(data$Sleep_Hours_Per_Day, 
                           breaks = c(4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, Inf), 
                           labels = c("4-5 hrs", "5-6 hrs", "6-7 hrs", "7-8 hrs", "8-9 hrs", "9+ hrs"), 
                           right = FALSE)

# 2. Create the box plot
ggplot(data, aes(x = Sleep_Category, y = GPA, fill = Sleep_Category)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.colour = "red", outlier.shape = 1) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3") + # Adds professional coloring
  labs(title = "GPA Distribution by Sleep Duration",
       subtitle = "Observed threshold effect around 8-9 hours of sleep",
       x = "Sleep Hours Per Day",
       y = "GPA") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") # Removes legend as labels are already on the X-axis

# 3. Optional: Print the exact medians to your console to verify
aggregate(GPA ~ Sleep_Category, data = data, median)
##   Sleep_Category  GPA
## 1        5-6 hrs 3.11
## 2        6-7 hrs 3.10
## 3        7-8 hrs 3.12
## 4        8-9 hrs 3.13
## 5         9+ hrs 3.08
